problem:
Consider the differential equation 

$$
{y}^{″}+4y={x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

The corresponding homogeneous equation has the fundamental solutions ${y}_{1}(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)$ and ${y}_{2}(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x).$ 

Select the correct options in the reasoning below.

According to the method of variation of parameters, we seek a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={{field-1}}
$$

where ${u}_{1}={u}_{1}(x),{u}_{2}={u}_{2}(x),$ that satisfies the constraint

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}(x)={{field-2}}.
$$

Differentiating ${y}_{p}$ with respect to $x,$ we obtain

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}(x)={{field-3}}.
$$
